notes.meaning: God allowed His people to become like dirt and garbage in the eyes of the surrounding nations. Their ruined city was despised by everyone around them, and other countries treated them as completely worthless.
Neighboring nations shouted insults against God's people and laughed at their fall. Because they hated the Jews, they openly rejoiced and spoke boldly against them without any fear.
The people found traps and sudden terrors waiting for them in every direction. Wherever they turned to escape danger, they met only ruin and deep sorrow.
The prophet weeps without stopping as he looks at the shattered state of his people. His sorrow is so deep that his tears flow down like rushing rivers.

The weeping will not stop until the Lord looks down from heaven and takes pity on His people. Even while crying endlessly, the faithful keep waiting on God, knowing only His help can change their situation.
Everything the prophet sees brings fresh pain to his soul. Looking upon the terrible suffering of the young women and villages of Jerusalem makes his grief even sharper.
Cruel enemies chased God's people like hunters chasing a defenseless bird. The people had done nothing to provoke this cruelty, yet their attackers pursued them without mercy.
The suffering was like being thrown alive into a deep, dark pit and sealed in with a heavy stone. All earthly hope seemed gone, as if the sufferers were buried alive and left for dead.
Troubles flooded over the speaker like deep water rising above his head. In that moment of weakness, it felt as though all life and hope had been completely cut off.
Even from the very lowest depths of distress, the believer cries out to the Lord in prayer. No pit or prison is so deep that God cannot hear the voice of His child calling on His name.
God had answered prayers in times past, and the speaker trusts Him to do so again. He pleads with the Lord not to close His ears to his quiet sighs and desperate groans for relief.
Whenever God's people call on Him, He draws close to comfort them. By calming their troubled spirits and answering their cries, the Lord reassures them not to be afraid.
The Lord steps in like a defender to fight for His servant when his life is on the line. Because God has rescued him from death before, he trusts that God will continue to protect him.
The Lord sees all the unfair treatment and cruelty His servant has suffered. Because God knows the true facts, the sufferer asks Him to act as judge and set things right.
God sees every hateful desire and secret plan that enemies make against His people. Nothing their opponents scheme in the dark is hidden from His sight.
The Lord hears every insult, slander, and whisper spoken against His servant throughout the day. Even when enemies conspire quietly, God listens to their threats and knows their evil intentions.
Everything the enemies do, from morning until evening, is filled with contempt for the sufferer. They make cruel jokes and sing mocking songs about his terrible pain.
The prayer asks God to give these cruel enemies the fair punishment their wicked actions deserve. God is asked to act as the righteous judge who repays people according to what they have done.
The speaker asks God to give these hard-hearted enemies deep blindness and sorrow of heart. He leaves them to the righteous curse that God has declared against unrepentant oppressors.

The final request is for the Lord to chase down and destroy these wicked oppressors from under His heavens. Their destruction will show everyone on earth that God sits on His heavenly throne as the true ruler and judge.
